A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ScoreLiDAR and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. All 21 pages of each version support comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original scene-completion experiments on SemanticKITTI and KITTI-360, ablations, occupancy evaluations, qualitative results, and a seven-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds EMD evaluations, keypoint-selection comparisons, and a semantic-completion experiment using SemCity.

M1.justification: The score-distillation objective, alternating student/auxiliary training, curvature-based keypoint selection, and structural-loss components are retained. The explicit nearest-neighbor formula matches v1's loss description. The 1/30 keypoint fraction and teacher-based initialization already appear in v1 Appendix A.3; their clarification does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: SemanticKITTI and KITTI-360 scene-completion coverage is retained. v2 Appendix D.7 adds a small semantic-completion evaluation using SemCity, extending task requirements beyond geometric completion. Its dataset is not explicitly identified, so an additional dataset cannot be established.

E2.justification: The main baseline set remains unchanged. v2 adds SemCity as an evaluated teacher/comparator in Table 14 and random and farthest keypoint selection in Table 9. Figure 4 removes the eight-step LiDiff qualitative comparison, although that comparator remains in the quantitative tables.

E3.justification: v2 introduces EMD evaluation, FID/KID for the SemCity experiment, and additional keypoint configurations. Section 4.3 corrects the stated keypoint fraction from 1/10 to 1/30, consistent with v1 Appendix A.3; this does not establish rerunning existing experiments. The newly specified sequence splits are additional disclosure, not evidence of changed splits.

E4.justification: Table 8 extends keypoint-count sensitivity from 1/30 and 1/60 to include 1/20 and 1/70. New Table 9 tests whether curvature-based selection improves on random and farthest selection. Existing loss-component, loss-weight, sampling-step, occupancy, user-study, and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experimental scores. The user-study sample of seven volunteers evaluating 30 scene pairs and its reporting practice are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands the results with EMD across benchmark and ablation tables, additional keypoint results, missing baseline runtimes, and semantic-completion scores. Table 14 reports ScoreLiDAR/SemCity FID of 81.76/88.52 and KID of 0.09/0.11. Added EMD reveals tradeoffs: refined ScoreLiDAR scores 23.26 versus LiDiff's 23.16 in Table 1, where lower is better. Existing CD/JSD, occupancy, and user-preference results are retained.

T1.justification: v2's Theoretical demonstration explicitly substitutes the score/noise relationship already given in v1 into the existing gradient approximation. Equation 12 expands the nearest-neighbor MSE already described in v1, and the VSD theorem discussion moves to Appendix F.1. These changes explain existing mathematics rather than introduce a substantive new definition, proof, or assumption.

C1.justification: The central structural-loss contribution and fivefold speedup claim remain. The introduction adds an explicit claim that existing acceleration techniques had not been explored for LiDAR completion. The conclusion replaces v1's conditional assertion about transferring semantic capability with preliminary experimental support and a qualification that more comprehensive exploration is required.

C2.justification: New Appendix B.1–B.2 substantially expands the mechanism explanations: teacher initialization, nonzero gradients after auxiliary updates, one-step training versus multistep inference, and using only one Chamfer-distance direction. v2 also explains increased EMD after refinement, adds the memory tradeoff for keypoint counts, and reframes the retained occupancy results as potentially affected by voxel-based evaluation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly specifies SemanticKITTI training sequences 00–07 and 09–10, evaluation sequence 08, and KITTI-360 evaluation sequence 00 without KITTI-360 training. v2 clarifies training/inference details and reports retraining SemCity and reproducing its metrics. It replaces the appendix's promised code release with stated model-and-code availability; actual availability is not independently established.

R1.justification: v2 broadens the score-guidance positioning through LucidDreamer, ScaleDreamer, and Taming Mode Collapse, and adds references supporting SemCity, EMD, and improved distribution matching. Two diffusion-training references previously cited in the limitations are removed. Most related-work coverage remains unchanged; venue abbreviations and publication updates are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: The introduction is rewritten around bidirectional gradient guidance, the discussion gains organized explanatory subsections, and appendix headings and cross-references change. Affiliations, corresponding-author information, and acknowledgements are updated. The main section sequence and most existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Many benchmark and ablation tables gain EMD columns, and new selection and semantic-completion tables are added. Figure 4 consolidates the earlier overview and appendix close-up presentation while removing two panels. Figure 1 and supplementary scene plates are reworked, additional close-ups appear, and the pipeline figure moves earlier. These substantially revise the presentation of comparisons.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through explicit sequence splits and resolves ambiguities in keypoint selection and training descriptions. New selection controls and EMD results strengthen assessment of the method's tradeoffs. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of the semantic pilot and new numerical inconsistencies: apparently corresponding refined ScoreLiDAR results have EMD 23.26 in Table 1 but 23.14 in Table 4. Overall, the clearer documentation and added evidence provide a modest net improvement.
